Regarding the definition of "zero-shot generalization" in the context of text-to-image AIs, it seems sensible. The concept of zero-shot generalization refers to the ability of a model to apply its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts without requiring additional training data. In the context of text-to-image AIs, this means that the model can generate images based on text prompts without having seen the specific images or concepts before.

The 2013 paper cited in the response likely discussed the concept of zero-shot generalization in the context of deep learning and neural networks, and how it applies to text-to-image AIs. The definition seems to align with the capabilities of modern text-to-image AIs, which can generate images based on text prompts and adapt to new concepts and styles.

However, it's worth noting that the definition may not be universally applicable, and there may be nuances and limitations to zero-shot generalization in text-to-image AIs. For example, the model may not always be able to generalize to new concepts or styles, especially if the training data is limited or biased. Nevertheless, the definition provides a useful framework for understanding the capabilities and limitations of text-to-image AIs.
